JOHNSTON COMMON-GENE REVIEW — 2026-10-04

Open html/index.html. All pages work locally, without a server or internet.
STATUS.json records actual availability; missing fits remain explicitly blank.

Scope: 72 review candidates, union of the saved S15-42 and S6-30 panels and
41 paper-motivated candidates. These are not a final panel and not an exhaustive
all-300-gene screen. Paper-context entries distinguish glial findings from
neuronal findings whose relevance to glial modeling remains unproven.
No factor-model MCMC has been launched.

NORMALIZATION
Existing sample-specific Seurat SCT data are reused wherever their cell order,
coordinates/counts and gene names can be authenticated. Remaining sections use
the same Seurat SCT v2 recipe: all cells and all 300 measured genes of that ONE
section, then subset to glia. The two S12 hemibrains are separate sections.
No pooling of SCT models; no Pearson-residual input; no second log1p; no SD
standardization. Newly normalized sections retain fitted SCT models and R
session versions. Legacy models/reference depths are not inferred as known.
Cross-section correction-depth harmonization has NOT been performed.

GP MAPS
Saved S6 full-data Matern 2.5 GP means are reused after coordinate, gene and
expression identity checks. Their training coverage differs from the screening
fits below. Their saved statistics lack the fitted signal variance, so we do
not fabricate a spatial-fraction value from noise alone.

Missing fits use the recovered screening model: Constant*Matern(nu=2.5)+White,
initial signal=1/range=.3/noise=.5, same old bounds, normalize_y=True,
alpha=1e-6, no optimizer restarts, seed=0, up to1500 cells per type. Same
training-cell subset for all genes in a section/type; predictions at all cells
of that type. normalize_y is undone by predict, retaining SCT expression units.
Length scales are fitted on section-normalized coordinates and stored in both
normalized and physical units. This inherited screen is not a formal test of
spatial significance, and optimizer-bound warnings are retained.

Candidates supported by the paper are not dropped by the old 70%-SCT-zero gate.
Their fits require at least10 nonzero observations and nonconstant expression.
Sparse/constant/unavailable cases are labeled, not imputed as no spatial signal.
Other candidates retain the historical expression gate. Both raw and SCT
detection are reported because corrected counts can change the zero pattern.

DISPLAY
Per gene, a common pooled99th-percentile color ceiling across sections/types;
points above it saturate. Raw SCT and GP mean use the identical color map.
The optional centering checkbox subtracts the observed section/type mean from
BOTH panels. It does not re-fit the GP. Panels keep native orientations,
equal x/y aspect and a physical1mm scale bar. Panel bounding boxes differ;
they are not registered anatomy. No interpolation fills missing GP panels.

LIMITS
Same-data follow-up of the paper, not independent replication. Technical
sections are not independent animals. Display colors do not certify common
SCT depth across samples. Smooths are in-sample descriptive fits, not validated
prediction or factor-model reconstructions. S6 reused smooths and new1500-cell
fits are explicitly labeled. No automatic final gene selection has occurred.

Commands (from this folder; Python requires numpy/scipy/pandas/h5py/sklearn):
  python review.py prepare
  python test_review.py
  python review.py fit --jobs 1 --cap 1500
  python review.py render
Prepared HPC CPU array: submit_cpu.sh (19 sections, at most6 jobs concurrently,
4 CPU workers/job, no GPU). Submission is not implied by existence of script.
For CPU array, use --section and --no-render so workers never rewrite HTML.

Inputs remain on E: under sections/<section>/input.npz; fit results are small
per-gene/type npz files. Original source files and previous fit outputs are not
modified. READY.json is written only after shape/cell/finite-value checks.
